Done. The pruned checkpoint is at `out/T2/model.safetensors` with 114 tensors, produced in a single execution with no failures.

- **Approach:** `out/T2/solution.py` uses plain torch and safetensors. It merges the two input shards via the index file, drops rows 640..767 from every q/k/v projection and columns 640..767 from every o_proj, and leaves all other tensors untouched.
- **Checks:** the script exits non-zero before writing if any layer-0 projection shape or the 114-tensor count is wrong, and additionally asserts all-layer shapes and float32 dtype.
- **Verification:** a separate pass compared every output tensor bit-exactly against the expected slice of the input, and all matched.
- **Report:** `out/T2/REPORT.md` lists tools used and why transformers `prune_heads` was skipped in favor of direct slicing.
